items.note: S2.4.1 gives the eight-row copy/gather/scatter/side-injection schedule, y_S += x_S for arbitrary scratch values, and (X_a,Y_a) -> (-Y_a,X_a) with every scratch wire restored. But 'three such stages' drops the fact that stage 2 runs the inverse schedule from Y to X (lines 731-733, 761-763). There is no derivation: the net change (JV+RG)x and the composition (x,y)->(x,y+x)->(-y,y+x)->(-y,x) are missing, and S2.4.3.1 only alludes to the cancellation of coefficients.

The plan follows the paper's route: a common frame commutes with the pointwise gate (line 812), frames telescope along a route, the result is D_out S_Omega D_in^{-1}, and intermediate frames are free to make edges cheap. The route operator in S2.4.2.2 omits the scalar sign epsilon_w (lines 820-822), and the parent S2.4.2 writes D_out D_in^{-1} without the routing S_Omega.

S2.4.3.2 and S2.4.3.3 state the lemma exactly: comparable labels, the only decreasing edges are central 3->4 losing h, L=Ich, sum of |change| = Wm-2N+2L, and L/N = 100/539 and 101/539. S2.4.3.1 supplies the orthogonality of neighbouring triple lines. Missing from the derivation: the terminal labels (U_a, F, U_a^perp), the gate-label table, the residual table, and the telescoping that makes the signed sum Wm-2N from source dimensions N and sink dimensions Wm-N (lines 881-897, 1066-1071).

The rank sum s_b = W_b m - N + 2L_b < W_b m is derived exactly as in the paper: rank(P_V - P_U) = dim V - dim U, plus N rank-one source exceptions (2P_{U_a}). 'Endpoint matrices differ by I_m' does not say that the difference is M_sink(rho(w)) - M_source(w), and the plan never introduces the frames Phi_M that turn it into H <- H+D. The computation P_{U_a^perp} - (-P_{U_a}) = I_m (lines 1169-1171) is missing.

S2.4.3.5 gives one kernel aI+bX_v per orthonormal residual vector and s_c = W_c m - 2N + 2L_c < W_c m. It omits the inverse kernels, the phase frames C_U, and the conclusion that diagonal corrections give C^{tensor m} on every role. It is an infer step with no derivation (the weight-additivity mod 4 and Hadamard-conjugation argument is absent).

The chain L/N < 1/2 => deficit N-2L > 0 => s < Wm, then deficits > 20*2^-50 and log m < 20 => s/W < m^tau with tau = sigma = 1-2^-50, is all present. The explicit eta_b and eta_c values and the inequality m^{1-2^-50} = m exp(-2^-50 log m) > m(1-20*2^-50) > m(1-eta) (lines 1331-1338) are not shown; S2.4.4 only asserts the conclusion.

S2.2 lists the four elementary O(V) operations correctly. S2.3 drops the condition that the offset is prepared in b^{O(1)} time, Q = q^b with q prime, and the fixed rational-unit scalings. Its one-line mechanism says the split is 'at the offset', whereas the paper splits at Q-a (line 577).

The factorization A = E_1 Pi E_2, triangular work done as controlled shifts, and one interchange per one of Pi via D_j += H_i, swap, D_j <- H_i - D_j all match the paper. The statement omits that the shear is over Z/q^b for a fixed odd prime q. The derivation omits that choice of q (avoiding denominators and diagonal numerators, so the factors stay invertible mod q^b) and the elimination proof of the factorization (lines 1375-1392, 1413-1423).

The plan follows the paper's route: cyclic row split into W role streams of volume V/W, the middle of three shears done by the network with each edge done by recursive interchanges, exactly s calls, an O(V) fixed-tape schedule, F_0 = O(1), F_k <= (s/W)F_{k-1} + O(1), and the geometric sum split into a <= 1 and a > 1, giving F_k = O(e^tau). That the frames yield H <- H+D on every row is left implicit (it comes from S2.4.2 and S2.4.3.4).

The statement matches the lemma: (p,h,g,d,z) -> (p,d,g,h,z) in O(Vu^tau). The sub-steps follow the proof: the top rho digits supply the row field, padding to a multiple of W^k rows, base-m expansion of the remaining width into power-width calls, and binary padding to [q^e] with e = O(u). The unequal-width remark (lines 1740-1762) is not covered.

The following are correct: the C identities, the GL(m,F_2) change of basis per column putting residual directions in slots, exactly s_c children on e/m axes, (C^-1)^{tensor f} = (-i)^f Z C Z, and H_0^{tensor D} = b^D S_D C^{tensor D} S_D. Missing: the decomposition of P_M into a fixed number of row additions (lines 1892-1901) and the endpoint Z_{a,f} and i^{27f} corrections that make the result C^{tensor e} on every role (lines 1907-1913). S2.6.1 also loosely calls each factor 'C = aI+bX' instead of aI+bX_v or its inverse.

The time bound with delta_bad = min{1, 80(f-1)2^-K}, the eight-operation parity flip, the bad set with |B| <= delta_bad M, and the radix-sort repair are all correct and follow the proof. Two parts are absent. The first is that each rotation is a controlled shift after chunk swaps bring the target after its controls; this is the source of the L^tau term (lines 2117-2155). The second is that S_0 and T_0 both preserve B, so T_0 S_0^{-1} permutes only B (lines 2107-2114).

These are correct: rows from the first q_0 chunks, the u = Wg+w split giving 1/W volume, the recurrence with leaves O(e) for e < d^beta, internal costs O(e^lambda), leaves O(e^sigma d^{beta(1-sigma)}), and lambda' > max{lambda, sigma+beta(1-sigma)}. The derivation lacks the step K <= d^c <= e^{c/beta} at internal nodes, which uses tau(1+c/beta) < lambda to bound the (eK)^tau overhead by e^lambda (lines 2413-2415).

The statement is right: Q_p(Hz) in O(Vd^{lambda'}), error < sqrt2 2^-p, unit disk, exact evaluation before one truncation, guard width ceil(C_0 d^{C_1}) = o(p). S2.6 says 'd address chunks' where the paper allows D <= d. The guard width is only asserted: the depth recurrence A(e) <= sA(e/m) + E and its unrolling (lines 2479-2573) are absent, as is the uniformity check on packed costs (lines 2696-2735).

The following are correct and follow the paper: character cancellation, the decimation-in-frequency step with twiddle omega_t^-k, the bit-reversed storage B_t, rounds grouped as a parallel butterfly followed by J_E, and the layout and cost bound. Missing: why the reverse procedure equals F_t^+ B_t^{-1} (H_0^2 = I/2 and the composite I/t, lines 2872-2887). The layout cost is only asserted in S3.2; the Dq-1 exchanges at O(TpK^tau) each are not shown.

The plan follows the paper: evaluation at B_0 = 2^{4p}, four products with the established multiplier, the separation |h_j| <= r2^{2p} < 2^{3p} < B_0/2, centred-residue extraction with a carry in {0,1}, negacyclic reduction, and the disk bound. Encoding details are omitted but no essential step is.

The error and cost statement is exact. The route (forward transforms in a common LB order, pointwise products commuting with the record permutation, normalization via F^+F^- = I/M) is present. The error propagation (2delta+eta, then 3delta+eta, scaled by M) and the final exact scaling by M are only asserted ('its error and cost are the stated ones').

Correctly stated: P_sF_s = 2^{2alpha^2} B_0 P_t F_t A under theta > p/alpha^4, error < p^2 (in units of 2^-p) and cost O(tp^{3/2+delta}alpha), the tensor form with gamma = 2d alpha^2, and the linewise and axis-exposure costs. The definitions of P_s and P_t ((P_su)_j = u_{tj}, (P_tv)_k = v_{-sk}) are never given. The derivation through the Gaussian maps S, T, the selection C, the diagonal D and the Neumann series (lines 3576-3640) is absent; the sub-steps are results only.

Both identities are stated correctly: QF_t u = conj(a).(a*(conj(a).u))/T with the stated chirp, and (RF_s^+)[(RF_s u)(RF_s v)] = (u*v)/S^2. Both are infer steps without derivation, and getting RF_s^+ by conjugation is not mentioned.

These are right: the fixed exponents, the sizes b, p, d, K, T, the prime-interval count, (1-2eta)t_i < s_i <= (1-eta)t_i, T/2 < S < T, and alpha^4 theta_i > p. Missing: delta = 1/16 from the fixed choice, eta = 1/(4d), alpha = ceil((12d^2 b)^{1/4}), gamma <= b/4, and the n^{o(1)} prime search. The computations S/T > (1-1/(2d))^d > 1/2 and alpha^4 theta_i > 3db >= p are not shown.

Phi: x -> prod x_i^{mu_i} with mu_i = P_i^{-1} mod s_i is shown to be an isomorphism (the image of x has order S). The triangular mixed-radix formula, the implementation by controlled shifts plus O(d^2) axis moves, and the cost O(Tp d^2(1+l^tau)) follow the paper. The descending update order and the treatment of the padded box are left implicit.

The exact algebra is right: Theta is diagonal (multiply coefficient k by zeta^k) and the wrap check gives zeta^{k+l}(-1)^h = zeta^j. Missing: the linewise interface M_C(f,g) = D_- iota^{-1} M_r(iota D_+ f, iota D_+ g) = (f*g)/T, and the computed twist with its 2*2^-p phase errors and truncations (lines 4349-4413).

The plan follows the paper's six steps: Phi, two source transforms (A, chirp, B_0, then 2^gamma, with exact counterpart RF_s), pointwise product, the opposite transform, scaling by S and by 2^{2b+4}S, rounding, Phi^{-1}, and carries. It also explains why the two occurrences of S undo different normalizations. The input scale 2^{-b-2} and the conjugation definition of F^+ are only implicit.

These are correct: the norms .26 and < .5, E_w = S(3E_s+2) < 28*2^gamma T^2 L, the final 448b 2^{-b+gamma} <= 448b 2^{-3b/4} < 1/2, unique rounding into [0,2^{3b}), and the carry invariant. The source-error constant E_s = 9*2^gamma TL and its chain through the ring and chirp errors (lines 4641-4657) are not given, nor is gamma <= b/4.

All seven table rows, their powers of p, the margins g_1..g_7 with min g_2 = eps c(1-tau) = 2^-181 = 2kappa, and the absorption of log powers into p^kappa are correct. The plan omits the paper's accounting that setup across recursion visits and exceptional-stream sorting are o(V) (lines 4913-4981), and the schoolbook cutoff for small n (lines 4989-4991).
S1 alludes to Schonhage and Strassen's n log n order but never states the eventual lower bound T_A(n) >= c_A n lg n or why one machine with liminf T_A(n)/(n lg n) = 0 refutes it.

errors.says: Since Harvey and van der Hoeven met the n log n order, a further saving must beat a logarithmic factor by a power.
errors.paper: The paper only records that Harvey and van der Hoeven reached O(n log n) and that it obtains a strict power saving in the logarithmic factor. It does not claim that any further improvement must be a power saving.

errors.says: The controlled shift splits each fiber at the offset and merges the two pieces in the opposite order.
errors.paper: Each fiber's Q blocks are split at Q-a, and the merge reads the second piece and then the first. The claim also drops the condition that the offset is prepared in b^{O(1)} time.

errors.says: The fixed exchange network has W wires of rank-m labels.
errors.paper: Labels are nondegenerate subspaces of the m-dimensional space F^{tensor 3}, with dimensions from 0 to m. Only the ambient space has dimension m.

errors.says: Three such stages exchange the banks (X_a,Y_a) -> (-Y_a,X_a).
errors.paper: Stages 1 and 3 are forward invocations from X to Y, but stage 2 runs the inverse forward schedule from Y to X, giving X <- X-Y. Three identical forward stages would not exchange the banks.

errors.says: The array network applies only the endpoint operator D_out D_in^{-1} to each role.
errors.paper: The implemented operator is D_out S_Omega D_in^{-1}. The route from w goes to rho(w) and carries the scalar sign epsilon_w.

errors.says: A route from role w to role rho(w) applies D_sink(rho(w)) D_source(w)^{-1} to its array.
errors.paper: The route applies epsilon_w D_sink(rho(w)) D_source(w)^{-1}. The sign matters for the complex network, whose exchange is (X,Y) -> (-Y,X).

errors.says: Indicator vectors of triples satisfy <t_S,t_T> = |S cap T|-1, so triple lines are nondegenerate and neighbours orthogonal. Gather and scatter coefficients depend on the intersection and side wires cancel the rest.
errors.paper: The formula holds only for the bit network's rational form x^T(I-J/9)y. The complex network uses the F_2 dot product with t.t = 1. The coefficient-cancellation clause comes from the scalar-network proof, not from the quoted label line.

errors.says: H_0 is applied at the same bit offset in d address chunks.
errors.paper: The layer acts on D consecutive chunks with 1 <= D <= d.

errors.says: Each edge of the complex network factors into one two-point kernel C = aI+bX per residual basis vector.
errors.paper: Each factor is a translation kernel aI+bX_v along the residual vector v, or its inverse.

chain: The tree follows the paper's route to O(n(lg n)^{1-kappa}): the two tape procedures come from the rank-saving networks (S2), feed the synthetic transforms and the ring convolution (S3) and Gaussian resampling with the retained permutations (S4), and the assembly ends in the margin table (S5.7). The movement half (S2.4-S2.5) is the most complete branch. The chain thins where results are only asserted: the label construction and the endpoint identity, the one-dimensional resampling identity (no Gaussian maps), the guard-width depth bound of the butterfly layer, the source-error constant E_s, and the o(V) setup accounting.

steps.note: S2.4.1 carries the mechanism: an eight-row network whose stages give (X_a,Y_a) -> (-Y_a,X_a) and restore every scratch wire. The defining parameters are missing (h=100, the triple indexing of X_a,Y_a, N = binom(h,3)^3 and m = h^3), and 'three such stages' hides the inverse middle stage. Conservative verdict.

The common frame commutes with the pointwise gate, the network implements D_out S_Omega D_in^{-1}, and each edge pays only D_v D_u^{-1}, with intermediate frames free to make edges cheap. The sign epsilon_w is omitted.

Nested nondegenerate subspaces of F^{tensor 3} are attached to gates and terminals, and every edge joins comparable labels. The only decreasing edges are central 3->4, each losing h. The dimension m and the label table are not given explicitly.
rank(P_V - P_U) = dim V - dim U, unchanged by reversing the edge. The N negative source projections are the exceptions, each with a rank-one first edge.
L = Ich and the sum of |change| = Wm-2N+2L, so s_b = W_b m - N + 2L_b. The telescoping that gives Wm-2N is not shown, but the budget itself is stated in its role.
L_b/N = 100/539 and L_c/N = 101/539 are both below 1/2, so the deficit N - 2L_b > 0 and s_b < W_b m.

S2.4.3.4 gives endpoint matrices differing by I_m on every input role, with the -P_{U_a} sources named in S2.4.3.4.2. S2.4.6.2 uses the network as the middle shear H <- H+D. This is loose: the identity is not written as M_sink(rho(w)) - M_source(w), and the shear frames Phi_M are never named.
A = E_1 Pi E_2 with lower triangular factors, exactly a interchanges plus O(V) (one per one of Pi), and exactly s recursive calls per node.
Role streams have volume V/W and F_k <= (s/W)F_{k-1} + O(1). From deficits > 20*2^-50 and log m < 20, s/W < m^tau with tau = 1-2^-50, and the geometric sum gives F_k = O(e^tau).

central.summary: The plan rebuilds the central saving almost entirely: frames, nested labels, rank equal to dimension change with the N source exceptions, the budget Wm-2N+2L, L/N < 1/2, the endpoint identity, edges as recursive calls, and the recurrence with tau = 1-2^-50. That gives 8 of 9 steps reconstructed. Only the fixed network itself (C1) lacks its defining parameters h=100, N and m, though its exchange-and-restore mechanism is stated.
